title: Lesson 35 - Calculated Insights in Practice: Dimensions, Measures, and Where Results Are Used
description: Demonstrate how to enhance data and build insights on unified data., focused on building a calculated insight in practice: choosing its base object, defining measures and dimensions, picking the metric level, and the places a calculated insight result can be used.

questions.question: A calculated insight must produce one lifetime value per customer for a personalization attribute. What must the insight group by?
options: The Individual dimension so each row is a person
No dimension, for a single overall total
questions.explanation: Grouping by the Individual dimension yields one row per person, which is the form a profile-level metric and personalization attribute require, while category or date groupings describe groups rather than people.

questions.question: Which pair correctly defines a measure and a dimension in a calculated insight?
options: Measure is the field you group by; dimension is the metric function
Measure is the metric function applied to a field; dimension is the attribute you group the measure by
Both are metric functions applied to the base object
Measure is a page layout; dimension is a record type
questions.explanation: A calculated insight computes a measure, a metric function applied to a field, grouped by dimensions, the grouping attributes, so the options that swap these roles or use non-insight concepts are wrong.

questions.question: Which statement about where a calculated insight result can be used is TRUE?
options: It exists only for display and cannot be consumed elsewhere
It publishes a reusable insight object that segment criteria, personalization attributes, copy field enrichments, and data graphs can read
It can be used once and is then discarded
It serves as a replacement for identity resolution
questions.explanation: The insight object is reusable across segment criteria, attributes, enrichments, and data graphs, so re-running the definition updates consumers, and it is not display-only, single-use, or a substitute for identity resolution.
